title: How do you generate 2D animations using AI?
author: Icy-Class-3793
selftext: I'd really like to know what AI tools you're using to easily generate characters and animations.

comments.author: Vindelator
comments.body:
This is the best I've seen so far:  
[https://www.pixellab.ai/create-character](https://www.pixellab.ai/create-character)

Another option is to use google flow to animate an illustration or something. Then, download the mp4 and extract the frames. (possibly scale them up to look cleaner, ditch the backgrounds and scale to the right size). It's not perfect or lossless and probably wrong for pixel art. I tried doing that for a while. Makes for interesting animation at least.

comments.body: diseño los personajes en gemini y los animo en ludo y le aplico filtros para que no parezca un collage todo raro

comments.author: fallaxmallum
comments.body: best i could do was create 3d render of image i want to animate, generate a short video of animation and then extract useful frames to use as 2d animation.. difficult part is getting ai to create the video you want..especially without background noise. talk about hair pulling experience (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻

comments.author: Muted_Tie_5902
comments.body: There’s a bunch of different ways you can kind of prompt using nano banana I find it’s the best to prevent drift and stick to structure but it still hit and miss. I use grimoire locally and they have an animate anything local model which can make some decentish stuff but you need the compute to run it.

replies.body: If I may ask what is grimoire? Would it be possible to run it at 12 gb vram?

comments.author: Timely_Extent_423
comments.body: Sprit sheets plus a rigging tools like spine gets you further than pure video generation, I ran into that tradeoff early. mage space is one place people batch character frames; Spine handle the actual animation logic

comments.author: drunnells
comments.body: I probably did it the hard way. I used Google Flow after I had the character look that I wanted for a reference image and prompted for the animation. Once I had that I resized the video and turned it into a series of still images with ffmpeg and then had codex write a script to remove the background from each frame. From there I took the frames I wanted and made a traditional sprite sheet.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
So the main issue with using a standard AI tool like Google Nano Banana for 2d assets like spritesheet animations is that those models can't output transparency, and models like GPT image gen and nano banana have no concept of animation frames, movement, and alignment between frames. You'll spend more time cleaning up the output than you saved generating it.

https://i.redd.it/oyzxc8te8xoh1.gif

I actually ran into this enough that I ended up building [Gamelabs Studio](https://gamelabstudio.co/ai-sprite-sheet-generator?ref=reddit.com) . It handles transparent spritesheets, consistent angles/palette across frames, and tileable textures. It also has an MCP that you can use directly inside your coding agent
